magistrate: Judicial officer who handles certain legal cases, hearings, warrants, or local court matters.
sweetness: Quality of having a sugary taste, or a gentle and pleasing character or manner.
toddler: Very young child who has recently learned to walk but is not yet school age.
entree: Main dish of a meal in North America, or an opening course in some other traditions.
calamity: Serious event causing widespread damage, suffering, or misfortune.
biologist: Scientist who studies living organisms and the processes that sustain life.
armament: Weapons and military equipment available to a force, vehicle, or country.
guitarist: Musician who plays the six-stringed or related instrument by plucking or strumming.
anthropologist: Researcher who studies human societies, cultures, origins, and ways of life.
meter: Device for measuring a quantity, or metric unit of length equal to one hundred centimeters.
gunshot: Discharge of a firearm, or the sharp sound produced when it is fired.
prophecy: Statement believed to predict a future event, often through religious or supernatural insight.
fielder: Player whose role is to catch, stop, or return the ball while the opposing side is batting.
gallbladder: Small organ beneath the liver that stores bile and releases it during digestion.
chemist: Scientist who studies substances, their properties, reactions, and transformations.
broadcaster: Person or organization that transmits radio, television, or online programs to an audience.
drugstore: Retail shop selling medicines along with health, beauty, and everyday household products.
hippocampus: Brain structure important for forming memories and navigating spatial surroundings.
centenary: Hundredth anniversary of an event, institution, or person’s birth.
shortstop: Baseball infielder positioned between second and third base, covering a large central area.
genus: Biological rank grouping closely related species below a family and above a species.
rain: Water droplets falling from clouds when condensed moisture becomes heavy enough to descend.
mania: Period of unusually elevated energy and mood, or an intense enthusiasm for a particular thing.
poultry: Domesticated birds such as chickens, turkeys, or ducks raised for meat or eggs.
cologne: Light scented liquid worn on the skin, generally less concentrated than perfume.
blizzard: Severe snow event with strong winds, low visibility, and dangerous travel conditions.
councillor: Elected or appointed member of a local governing body or advisory council.
munitions: Military supplies used in weapons, including bullets, shells, bombs, and related explosive items.
motorway: High-speed divided road designed for long-distance traffic with controlled access.
saxophonist: Musician who plays the keyed wind instrument commonly heard in jazz and popular music.
ballot: Paper, electronic choice, or voting process used to record a person’s selection in an election.
asphalt: Dark petroleum-based material mixed with aggregate and used to surface roads and paths.
narrator: Voice or character that tells the events of a story to the audience.
electrophoresis: Laboratory method that separates charged molecules by moving them through a medium with electricity.
bidder: Person or company that offers a price in an auction or submits an offer for a contract.
proton: Positively charged particle found in the nucleus of nearly every atom.
keyboardist: Musician who plays piano, synthesizer, organ, or another instrument operated with keys.
archaeologist: Specialist who studies past societies through objects, buildings, graves, and other material remains.
raindrop: Single bead of water falling from a cloud.
